PhotoLifecycle alone issues handles, camera compression consumes that handle, and deletion/sweep share canonical exact-parent, regular-file, app-prefix ownership checks. Fresh 18-test JVM, forced build/lint, two 4-test SM_F711N runs, multipart/cancel/cap/timeout/concurrency/EXIF probes, and an independently repeated four-state PID-changing restart all pass with complete cleanup.

evidence: PhotoLifecycle.ManagedPhoto has a private Kotlin source constructor; its internal companion factory accepts only a PhotoLifecycle and creates the temp file itself under that lifecycle's private cache directory.
PhotoLifecycle.createManagedPhoto() takes no caller File or directory argument.
PhotoLifecycle no longer exposes createCacheFile(), manage(File), fileProviderUri(File), or compressCamera(File).
Normal reflection/API regression found no public non-synthetic source constructor and no public compressCamera(File) method.

javap confirms the primary (File, File) constructor is private. Kotlin also emits its standard synthetic DefaultConstructorMarker bridge; this is a compiler implementation detail excluded from the supported source/API surface, not an ordinary caller construction path.
fileProviderUri and compressCamera accept only ManagedPhoto.

Fresh SM_F711N native-contract test created a lifecycle handle, wrote a real 32x32 JPEG, verified TakePicture EXTRA_OUTPUT used its FileProvider URI, compressed through compressCamera(handle), and observed the owned source absent afterward.
Fresh JVM regression proves the former raw File method is absent and a persistent-camera.jpg foreign file survives.
ManagedPhoto.delete re-canonicalizes both the candidate and dedicated directory at deletion time.
Deletion requires candidate.isFile, exact canonical parent equality, and leftovers-photo- app prefix before deleting.
ownedCacheFiles uses the same regular-file, exact-parent, app-prefix checks through ownedFile; sweep consumes only that filtered list.
Canonical exact-parent equality rejects traversal and path-string prefix confusion; a symlink resolving outside the managed directory fails parent equality, and directories fail isFile.
Fresh JVM tests remove a 25-hour managed file, preserve a 23-hour managed file, preserve an old prefix-free file inside leftovers-photos, and preserve an old file outside that directory.
Independent real restart reproduced all four states and observed stale owned absent while recent owned, unrelated inside, and unrelated outside remained present.
